category.description: Primary category of the desktop activity. file_operation: file explorer, save/open dialogs. network: web browsing, network settings. process: launching/closing applications. system_config: settings panels, control panel. data_access: viewing documents, database clients. authentication: login screens, credential prompts. other: anything not fitting above

start_time.description: The time that the first screenshot was taken in the event

end_time.description: The time that the last screenshot was taken in the event

risk_level.description: Context-aware risk level based on the event. Examples: opening a public website=none, accessing personal email=low, viewing confidential documents=high, displaying credentials=critical. Assess actual visible content not user intent

risk_score.description: Numeric risk score 0-100. Ranges: 0-20 benign, 20-40 low, 40-60 medium, 60-80 high, 80-100 critical

threat_category.description: Primary MITRE ATT&CK tactic. Use 'none' for benign activity

timeline_title.description: Concise action summary. Focus on WHAT not HOW. Examples: 'Opened "finance-report.xlsx"', 'Browsed "github.com"', 'Launched Excel'. Max 10 words, main action only

timeline_subtitle.description: Empty string for routine activity. Only populate for notable failures or anomalies: 'Authentication failed', 'Permission denied', 'Connection error'. Max 4 words

short_description.description: One-line factual description without pronouns. Example: 'Opened the finance report in Excel' not 'User opened the finance report in Excel'

detailed_description.description: Detailed 1-2 line factual description. State actions observed, including the application, document or destination involved when visible. Avoid mere UI observations

suspicious_flags.description: Security-relevant actions observed on screen. Examples: opening a credentials manager, accessing internal admin tools, viewing sensitive system files. Exclude routine application use

sensitive_items.description: Sensitive files, documents, or data visible on screen. Examples: passwords, API keys, /etc/shadow, customer PII

suspicious_patterns.description: Patterns indicating malicious activity. Examples: rapid credential entry attempts, browsing known malicious domains, copying sensitive data to external destinations

iocs.description: Concrete indicators of compromise visible on screen: suspicious URLs, IP addresses, domain names, file hashes, or signatures

mitre_attack_ids.description: Specific MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs (e.g., T1059, T1055). Only technique IDs, not tactic names

has_sensitive_data.description: True if sensitive data was visible or accessed during the event

privilege_escalation.description: True if the event shows privilege escalation (e.g., UAC prompt accepted, sudo password entered, switching to an admin account)

data_exfiltration.description: True if data was transferred externally (e.g., uploading files, copying to webmail, posting to external sites)

persistence.description: True if persistence mechanisms were established (e.g., scheduling tasks, modifying startup programs, installing remote-access tools)

applications.description: Applications visible or interacted with during this event. Examples: 'Microsoft Excel', 'Google Chrome', 'PuTTY'

visible_urls.description: URLs visible on screen, e.g. browser address bars, links in emails, or terminal output

visible_file_paths.description: File paths visible on screen, e.g. in file explorer, save dialogs, terminals, or document titles

active_window_title.description: The title of the active/focused window during this event

notable_session_events.description: List of significant desktop session events observed across the screenshot batch
